$comment: Conformance vectors for DeepSeek's peak/off-peak billing rule. Public domain (CC0-1.0). Corrections welcome.

source.quote: Effective 00:00 (Beijing Time) on Sunday, August 23, 2026, we will adjust our peak/off-peak billing rules, with off-peak rates applying throughout the day on weekends.

deepseek-live-2026-08-23.note: DeepSeek's published schedule as of 2026-08-23. Peak windows are given in UTC; the calendar the weekend rule is read on is Asia/Shanghai.
deepseek-live-2026-08-23.peak_weekdays_note: ISO-8601 weekday numbers, 1 = Monday. Read on calendar_timezone, not on UTC. Both statements are load-bearing: an implementation that hard-codes Saturday and Sunday agrees with this field at all 168 hours of the live schedule, and one that reads the weekday off the UTC instant agrees with it everywhere except 16:00-24:00 UTC.

synthetic-overnight-peak.note: NOT a real vendor schedule. Its peak window deliberately covers 16:00-24:00 UTC, the only stretch where the UTC and Beijing calendars disagree. The live schedule cannot expose a wrong-calendar weekday read; this one can.
synthetic-overnight-peak.peak_weekdays_note: ISO-8601 weekday numbers, 1 = Monday. Read on calendar_timezone, not on UTC. Both statements are load-bearing: an implementation that hard-codes Saturday and Sunday agrees with this field at all 168 hours of the live schedule, and one that reads the weekday off the UTC instant agrees with it everywhere except 16:00-24:00 UTC.

vectors.why: inside the first daily peak window
the gap between the two daily windows

weekend overrides a daily peak window
weekend overrides the second daily window
before the rule took effect: not retroactive
last peak second before the rule took effect
the first instant the rule applies
UTC says Friday, Beijing says Saturday. Reading the weekday off the unshifted instant gives peak.
UTC says Sunday, Beijing says Monday. Reading the weekday off the unshifted instant gives offpeak.
UTC says Saturday, Beijing says Sunday: both calendars call it the weekend. Included so a failure on the two above cannot be blamed on the synthetic window itself.

next_boundary_vectors.why: Both sides of every boundary inside the weekend are off-peak, so the next real change is Monday 09:00 Beijing, about 63 hours out. A countdown that stops at the next window edge hits zero with nothing changing.
before the effective instant the weekend must not be skipped; the gate is on the candidate instant, not on 'now'
